title: Machine Learning Foundations
description: The learning problem, linear models, generalization, and gradient descent. Neural nets wait. Transformers wait longer.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS229 Machine Learning
sourceReferences.notes: Supervised setup and linear/logistic models before neural nets. No transformers in the core sequence. Linear algebra and probability are assumed tools, not LLM trivia.

modules.title: The learning problem
modules.blurb: Examples, features, and a loss you can actually compute.
learningObjectives: Name what a loss is for

modules.title: Linear models
learningObjectives: Fit a linear score by reducing a loss you can compute
Turn that score into a probability or a class without treating it as a promise

modules.title: Generalization
modules.blurb: Train, validation, test, and the ways you fool yourself.
learningObjectives: Split data so train, validation, and test keep three jobs
Diagnose a fit that memorized the sample instead of the population

modules.title: Optimization in practice
modules.blurb: Stochastic gradients and the assumptions underneath.
learningObjectives: Estimate a slope from a minibatch instead of the whole set
Name the i.i.d. assumption and a way real data violates it

concepts.name: The learning problem
concepts.summary: Inferring a rule from examples that should work on examples you have not seen.
objectives: State a learning problem as inferring a rule from examples that should work on unseen examples
Name what 'work' means here: a prediction job, not a memorized spreadsheet

concepts.name: Features and targets
concepts.summary: The inputs you chose and the thing you are trying to predict.
objectives: Separate the inputs you chose from the target you are trying to predict
Predict what breaks if the target leaks into the features

concepts.name: Hypothesis class
concepts.summary: The family of functions you are willing to consider.
objectives: Describe a hypothesis class as the family of functions you are willing to consider
Predict what a class that is too small or too large will do to the fit

concepts.name: Loss functions
concepts.summary: A number that says how wrong a prediction is.
objectives: Define a loss as a number that says how wrong a prediction is
Choose a loss that matches the prediction job rather than a leftover default

concepts.name: Vectors as the language of models
concepts.summary: Features live in a space. Geometry is not decoration.
objectives: Treat a feature vector as a point in a space, not a pile of columns
Read a weighted sum as a geometric operation in that space

concepts.name: Probability as bookkeeping
concepts.summary: Uncertainty written as numbers you can multiply.
objectives: Write uncertainty as numbers you can multiply and condition
Distinguish a probability from a decision you still have to make

concepts.name: Baselines before cleverness
concepts.summary: The dumb answer you must beat.
objectives: Name a dumb answer you must beat before claiming a model works
Predict when a clever model is losing to the mean or the majority class

concepts.name: Linear regression
concepts.summary: A weighted sum plus a bias, fit by reducing squared error.
objectives: Write a linear regression as a weighted sum plus a bias fit by reducing squared error
Predict the fit when one feature is a scaled copy of another

concepts.name: Logistic regression
concepts.summary: A linear score turned into a probability.
objectives: Turn a linear score into a probability with a logistic curve
Predict why a linear score alone is not a valid class probability

concepts.name: Predictions as probabilities
concepts.summary: A number between 0 and 1 is not a promise.
objectives: Treat a number between 0 and 1 as a calibrated claim, not a promise
Diagnose a confident probability that does not match observed frequency

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.summary: Following the slope of a loss you can actually compute.
objectives: Step parameters opposite the gradient of a loss you can compute
Predict what a step that is too large or too small does to the loss

concepts.name: Feature scaling
concepts.summary: Why unscaled inputs make the slope lie.
objectives: Rescale features so one column does not dominate the slope
Predict the crooked path gradient descent takes on unscaled inputs

concepts.name: Convex versus non-convex loss
concepts.summary: One bowl, or a landscape with many basins.
objectives: Distinguish a bowl with one minimum from a landscape with many basins
Predict why a local step is enough on a convex loss and not otherwise

concepts.name: Classification metrics
concepts.summary: Precision, recall, and why accuracy lies.
objectives: Compute precision and recall instead of trusting accuracy on a skewed set
Diagnose a high accuracy that still misses the class you care about

concepts.name: Train, validation, test
concepts.summary: Three splits, three jobs. Mixing them is the original sin.
objectives: Give train, validation, and test three different jobs and keep them unmixed
Name the original sin of tuning on the set you later report

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.summary: Fitting the sample, missing the population.
objectives: Describe overfitting as fitting the sample and missing the population
Read a training loss that falls while validation loss rises

concepts.name: Generalization
concepts.summary: Performance on the distribution, not the spreadsheet.
objectives: Define generalization as performance on the distribution, not the spreadsheet
Predict what a distribution shift does to a number you trusted on the test split

concepts.name: Bias and variance
concepts.summary: A model that cannot see versus a model that sees noise.
objectives: Contrast a model that cannot see the signal with one that sees the noise
Predict how more data or less capacity moves bias and variance

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.summary: Paying a tax on complexity so the fit cannot wander.
objectives: Tax complexity so the fit cannot wander as far as the sample would like
Choose an L2 or L1 penalty for a reason, not as a checkbox

concepts.name: Cross-validation
concepts.summary: Rotating the held-out slice when data is scarce.
objectives: Rotate the held-out slice when a single split is too noisy
Predict what leaks if you peek at the test fold while choosing a model

concepts.name: Model capacity
concepts.summary: How much structure the hypothesis class can represent.
objectives: Describe capacity as how much structure the hypothesis class can represent
Predict underfit and overfit from a capacity that is too small or too large

concepts.name: Early stopping
concepts.summary: Quitting while the validation loss is still honest.
objectives: Stop training when validation loss is still honest, before the sample is memorized
Predict why early stopping is a regularizer that needs a real validation split

concepts.name: Stochastic and mini-batch gradients
concepts.summary: Estimating the slope from a handful of examples.
objectives: Estimate the slope from a minibatch instead of the whole dataset
Compare full-batch, stochastic, and mini-batch updates on cost and noise

concepts.name: The i.i.d. assumption
concepts.summary: Independent, identically distributed — and how often that is a lie.
objectives: State the i.i.d. assumption: independent, identically distributed examples
Name a common way real data violates it and what that does to the split
